short: A bloody conflict sparked by Danish attempts to reclaim southern provinces lost to Sweden.
full:
Initiated by Denmark in 1675, the Scanian War was a direct attempt by King Christian V to recover the vital provinces of Scania, Halland, and Blekinge, which had been ceded to Sweden at the Treaty of Roskilde. The conflict was part of the wider Franco-Dutch War, with Sweden fighting as a French ally against Denmark and Brandenburg-Prussia. Early Danish naval victories severely disrupted Swedish communications and allowed a successful invasion of Scania.

The war on land devolved into brutal, attritional warfare, characterized by widespread guerrilla resistance from pro-Danish 'Snapphanar' partisans and scorched-earth tactics. Despite initial setbacks, the young King Charles XI rallied the Swedish army to decisive, bloody victories at Halmstad and Lund, halting the Danish advance. By 1679, the conflict ended in a strategic stalemate; French diplomatic pressure forced Denmark to sign the Treaty of Fontainebleau, restoring the pre-war borders and cementing Swedish control over its southern territories.
